zh:
【国风·秦风】

车邻

有车邻邻，有马白颠。未见君子，寺人之令。
阪有漆，隰有栗。既见君子，并坐鼓瑟。今者不乐，逝者其耋。
阪有桑，隰有杨。既见君子，并坐鼓簧。今者不乐，逝者其亡。

驷驖

驷驖孔阜，六辔在手。公之媚子，从公于狩。
奉时辰牡，辰牡孔硕。公曰左之，舍拔则获。
游于北园，四马既闲。輶车鸾镳，载猃歇骄。

小戎

小戎俴收，五楘梁辀。游环胁驱，阴靷鋈续。文茵畅毂，驾我骐馵。言念君子，温其如玉。在其板屋，乱我心曲。
四牡孔阜，六辔在手。骐駠是中，騧骊是骖。龙盾之合，鋈以觼軜。言念君子，温其在邑。方何为期？胡然我念之。
俴驷孔群，厹矛鋈錞。蒙伐有苑，虎韔镂膺。交韔二弓，竹闭绲縢。言念君子，载寝载兴。厌厌良人，秩秩德音。

蒹葭

蒹葭苍苍，白露为霜。所谓伊人，在水一方。溯洄从之，道阻且长。溯游从之，宛在水中央。
蒹葭萋萋，白露未晞。所谓伊人，在水之湄。溯洄从之，道阻且跻。溯游从之，宛在水中坻。
蒹葭采采，白露未已。所谓伊人，在水之涘。溯洄从之，道阻且右。溯游从之，宛在水中沚。
……
en:
[Odes: Qin]

Che Lin

His many chariots rush along,
Drawn by white-fronted steeds and strong.
When audience now we wish to gain,
His eunuchs' aid we must obtain.
The varnish trees on hill-sides grow,
And chestnuts on the lands below.
When access to the prince we've found,
We sit and hear the lutes' sweet sound.
If we seize not this joy to-day,
Old age will have us for its prey.
The mulberries on the hill-sides grow,
And willows where the grounds are low.
When to the prince our way we've made,
We sit and hear the organs played.
If we pass by this joy to-day,
Old age will bear us all away.

Si Tie

Our ruler to the hunt proceeds;
And black as iron are his steeds
That heed the charioteer's command,
Who holds the six reins in his hand.
His favourites follow to the chase,
Rejoicing in his special grace.
The season's males, alarmed, arise,
The season's males, of wondrous size.
Driven by the beaters, forth they spring,
Soon caught within the hunters' ring.
"Drive on their left," the ruler cries;
And to its mark his arrow flies.
The hunting done, northward he goes;
And in the park the driver shows
The horses' points, and his own skill
That rules and guides them at his will.
Light cars, whose teams small bells display,
The long and short-mouthed dogs convey.

Xiao Rong

Before my mind's eye stands my lord's short car,
In which he dares the risks of savage war:
Its pole, whose end turns upward, curving round,
And in five places shines, with leather bound;
The slip rings and the side straps; the masked place,
Where gilt rings to the front unite the trace;
The mat of tiger's skin; the naves so long;
The steeds, with left legs white, and piebalds, strong.
Such my lord's car! He rises in my mind,
Lovely and bland, like jade of richest kind;
Yet there he lives, in his log hut apart:
The very thought confuses all my heart.
The driver with the six reins guides along
The horses, with their shining coats, and strong:
One inside dappled, one bay with black inane;
Black-mouthed and bay, and black, the outer twain.
Shields, dragon-figured, rise up side by side,
Shelter in front 'gainst missiles to provide.
Gilt buckles with the carriage front connect
The inner reins by which the insides are checkt.
I see my lord, thus in his carriage borne,
With his mild form the frontier towns adorn.
What time can be for his return assigned?
Ah me! his figure ever fills my mind!
With measured steps move the mail-covered team.
The trident spears, with gilded shaft-ends gleam.
The feather-figured shield, of beauty rare,
He holds before him, all his foes to dare.
The bow-case, made of tiger's skin, and bright
With metal plates, lies ready for the fight.
It holds two bows which bamboo frames secure,
And keep unhurt, to send the arrows sure.
To him thus busy all my thoughts are borne,
Both when I rest at night and rise at morn.
He, my good lord, is tranquil and serene,
His virtuous fame more prized, the more he's seen.

Jian Jia

Reed and rush are dark and green;
As hoar-frost the white dew is seen.
Him, the person I have in mind,
By this water I should find.
Searching, up the stream I haste,
On a long and toilsome quest.
Downwards then I turn, and see!
In the mid-stream standeth he.
He is there but far removed;
Vain has all my searching proved.
Reed and rush luxuriant rise;
Still undried the white dew lies.
Him, the person I have in mind,
On the stream's edge I should find.
Upwards first my course I keep,
Though the way is rough and steep.
Downwards then, and what to see?
In the mid-stream standeth he,
On the islet, far removed;
Vain has all my searching proved.
Reed and rush grow thick and tall;
Ceases not the dew to fall.
Him, the person I have in mind,
On the stream's bank I should find.
Upwards first I go along,
But the hard path leads me wrong.
Downwards then my steps I turn,
And in mid-stream him discern,
On the island, far removed;
Vain has all my searching proved.

zh:
唐末以来，兵乱相继，为充国库，赋税繁重，致耕者不敢勤于劳作，更无力开垦荒田。赋役相循，百姓生业，每况愈下。
然今天下已定，陛下爱民，厉行节约，敦本抑末，使百姓得以安养，使汴京市井繁荣，足见陛下良策成效。
民虽居草野，仍常闻民生多艰，故陈策二端：
于民，可令能广植桑枣、开荒田者，只纳旧租，永不通检，以劝耕织；
于州县官吏，可嘉奖能招复逋逃，劝课栽植者，使旷土得耕，游民得业。

批：有理，采纳！待乱局平了，就将此二策能推行下去。此文为何人所作？速速请来！
en:
Since the late Tang, war and disorder have followed one upon another. To fill the coffers, taxes grew ever heavier, until those who tilled the land no longer dared labor in earnest, much less reclaim wasteland. Tax and corvée came one after the next, and the people's livelihood worsened by the day.
Yet now the realm has been brought to order. Your Majesty cherishes the people, practices frugality, and honors the root while restraining the secondary. Thus the people may live in peace, and the markets of Kaifeng flourish. This is proof enough of the success of Your Majesty's rule.
Though I dwell far from court, I still often hear of the hardships of common life. I therefore venture to submit two humble proposals:
For the people, let those who plant mulberry and jujube in abundance, or reclaim wasteland, pay only their former tax and never be reassessed thereafter, so as to encourage farming and sericulture.
For prefectural and county officials, let those who can call back runaways and fugitives, and promote cultivation and planting, be rewarded, so that abandoned land may be tilled again and the displaced regain their livelihood.

Note: Sound and well reasoned. Adopted. Once the turmoil has been settled, these two measures shall be put into effect. Who authored this memorial? Summon him at once.

The craftsmen worked tirelessly to save her. They never knew what she thought of it, and she never bothered to tell them.
Instead, like the curious children who watched the workshops, her mind was always drifting up into the clouds. How did the Mortise and Tenon fit so perfectly? How were those intricate machines built? The creaking of the water wheels made her heart itch with wonder.
The moon watched her that night, watched as she reached a chubby paw toward the spinning gears. Snap! Curiosity killed the cat.

zh:
四师姐其实是五师妹，池清浅才是同门五人中年纪最小的一个。个子小小，说话温吞吞的丫头总是习惯跟在师长们的身后，好像永远都会乖乖的。所有人都淡忘了，就是这个丫头，七岁就曾溜出山去采药，然后从山外背回了十岁的区彦希，那位年纪更大的五师弟。
外人都以为池清浅是不喜欢说话的，但在大师兄、二师兄、三师姐面前，她时不时就会滔滔不绝说个不停。上到天文地理，下到食材食性，她喜欢给师兄师姐们讲。而师兄师姐们都会停下手头的活计，认认真真地听。后来，又多了一个小师弟。
不知道是不是因为自己是他的救命恩人，他听讲时比其他三位师兄师姐还要认真。只是他总是一副有心事的样子，不肯，或者说不敢开口多问。最好的反馈，也只是开口笑一笑。
师父夸她是过目不忘的天才，但她知道，这个她背进山的小师弟，要比她更有天赋。她并不嫉妒，只是常常疑惑，为什么天赋异禀的小师弟的身上，总蒙着一层揭不开的雾呢？
类似这样想不通的事情真是太多了，她想不通三师姐明明喜欢二师兄，为什么就是不肯说呢？
二师兄也喜欢三师姐，为什么总是以轻佻的样子一笔带过，不痛不痒。
大师兄是机关人么？为什么永远都不会累呢？
师父为什么总要假装严肃？明明背地里，他在其他长老面前提起自己的弟子时就眉飞色舞，胡子飘飘。
师父明明最看重小师弟的天赋，为什么偏偏不肯将最精深的技艺传给他呢？
山里还有这么多有趣的事情，师兄师姐们为什么要叛出山去呢？墨山道不好吗？
太多想不明白的事情了，不懂就要去问。
山中封禁更严，临行之前，池清浅只去看了被关在悬空屋的小师弟。和小师弟隔着门告别的那晚，他第一次急得说了很多很多话，甚至放出了他的机关毒虫想要蛰晕她。但池清浅决定了的事，谁也拦不下来，从来如此。
十多年前她偷跑出山，救回了一个小师弟。这一次她偷跑出山，是为了师兄师姐们的一个答案。
后来，她找到了所有答案。遗憾的是，到最后她才发现，那答案不属于她。
和师兄师姐们并肩面对敌人的最后一次冲杀时，她突然想到一张憨憨笑着，认真听讲的脸。如果可能的话，大家都没有出山，该多好啊……
en:
Though addressed as "Fourth Sister," she was truly the fifth disciple. Chi Qingqian was the youngest of the five. A girl with a slow, gentle way of speaking, she seemed content to trail in the shadows of her seniors, forever the picture of obedience. It was easy to forget that this very girl, at age seven, had slipped away to gather herbs and hauled back a ten-year-old boy named Ou Yanxi, the boy who would become her "Junior" brother.
Outsiders thought Chi barely spoke. But around her senior siblings, she was endlessly talkative. From the mysteries of the stars to the hidden properties of roots and herbs, she loved to regale them with her knowledge. Maybe because she'd saved his life, he listened closer than the rest, yet always carrying himself with a burdened air, hesitant, or perhaps afraid, to ask a single question.
The Master praised her as a prodigy with a photographic memory, but she knew the boy she'd carried home possessed a talent that eclipsed her own. She wondered: why did this brilliant boy always seem shrouded in a mist that no wind could ever disperse? 
There were so many things she couldn't figure out. Why did Third Sister refuse to confess her feelings toward the Second Brother? And why did the Second Brother, who felt the same, always hide behind that mask of flippancy, keeping things so frustratingly light?
Was the First Brother actually an automaton? Did he truly never know exhaustion?
...
Too many questions. She needed answers.
Security in the mountains had become suffocating. Before her departure, Chi made one last visit to her junior brother, now imprisoned within the Aloft Abode.
The night they whispered their goodbyes through the heavy door, he panicked for the first time. Words poured out of him in a frantic torrent. He even unleashed his mechanical vipers, hoping to sting her into unconsciousness just to keep her from leaving. But once Chi set her course, she was as immovable as the mountain itself. It had always been so.
Over a decade ago, she had slipped away from the mountain to save a young boy who became her junior brother. This time, she slipped away again, driven by a need for answers from her senior brothers and sisters.
Eventually, she found every answer she sought. The tragedy was realizing, at the very end, that the answers were never hers to hold.
As she stood shoulder-to-shoulder with her seniors for the final, desperate charge, a face flickered in her mind, earnest and dorky, listening to her every word.
If only... If only we had all stayed. How wonderful it would have been if we'd never left the mountain at all.

绯云压岭不知年，野实垂枝欲坠肩。
山野有桃林，不知何人所植，立此数十载矣。春则花如绛雪，夏则实累青枝，百姓往来，采食作乐，不以为私。
细数此间桃品，颇有可观。红桃、绯桃、碧桃以色分者有之，御桃、方桃、绵桃以形名者有之。更有冬桃与霜桃等异熟诸品，依时而至，次第相迭。满谷之桃，经年不绝。
自某岁起，忽有恶匪啸聚，强据一方桃林。昔日野趣和乐之桃源，自此便换了人间。
今欲往者，匪徒之外，尚须留意头顶！观那桃实硕大，沉枝欲折。偶有熟落，砸地有声。行于树下，幸则避之，不幸则当头一记。
en:
Crimson clouds have long pressed over the ridge, and wild fruit hangs so heavy it seems to bow the branches to the shoulder.
Deep in the wilderness stands a peach grove, planted by no one knows whom, yet standing for decades. In spring, its flowers bloom like red snow; in summer, the fruit weighs down the green boughs. Commoners pass through freely, picking and feasting as they please, claiming nothing as their own.
The varieties here are well worth noting. There are those named by color: red peach, crimson peach, jade peach; those named by form: round peach, square peach, silken peach. Then there are the rare late-ripening kinds, such as winter peach and frost peach, each arriving in its own season, one following the other in succession. Throughout the whole valley, peaches yield without end through the year.
Yet at some point, a band of vicious outlaws gathered and seized a portion of the peach grove by force. What was once a joyful haven of wild freedom was changed utterly from that day forward.
Those who would venture there now must watch not only for bandits, but also overhead! The peaches grow large and heavy, bowing the branches near to breaking. Now and again a ripe one drops, striking the ground with a resounding thud. Walk beneath the trees, and you may be fortunate enough to step aside, or unfortunate enough to receive one squarely upon the head.

en:
Unusually large and intricately stitched, this pair of shoes bears the faded stains of bloody handprints. In the fierce struggle for the Peacock Crown, they were perhaps the closest thing to "eternity."
Sewn by a mother on a Kaiyuan morning, they were buried that afternoon, only to be unearthed by nightfall as their owner fled into exile. Washed when dirtied and mended when frayed, they journeyed endlessly. Year after year, they circled their hometown, yet never once dared to cross its borders.
Then, one morning, they stepped into this inn. That afternoon, they delivered an old friend's parcel to her room, and by nightfall, they finally came to rest.

一年没有、五年没有、许多年都没有。
现在，作为悬泉驿的最后一人，是该他去往长安的时候了。

Celestial Spring Station had received no news from the Tang in a long time. He hadn't either.

Wu Han handed over the maps he'd drawn and began to wait for his return.

But his friend didn't come back for years.
Now, as the last person at the Celestial Spring Station, it was his turn to go to Chang'an.

However, he still didn't make it to Chang'an. He died at the hands of the Utuk.

zh:
在外漂泊这些年，王大犬也时常给家里去信。阿婆腿脚不好，眼神也不好，都要靠邻里帮忙读信。
偶有几封回信到王大犬手里。可拆开来，内容都是阿婆的絮叨——多添饭，多穿衣。
阿婆说，他知道大犬是个好孩子，能干，麻利，会好好照顾自己。
每次和信一起到的，都有一个小小的包袱。里面是阿婆的馍。王大犬在信里反复说，天高路远，馍到了都干了嚼不动。可阿婆却依然会在回信的时候蒸上馍，一起捎给她离家最远的孩子。
王大犬只好把干掉的馍丢掉。毕竟，江南风情旖旎，什么样的美食珍馐吃不到呢。
直到那一天，一封加急书信传来。

王大犬不知道，在自己离家后不久，阿婆就摔伤了腿，几个月都卧床难下。
多亏婶娘照看，阿婆才不至于饿死家中。
那是个寻常的晚上。阿婆睡不着，总觉着后背烧着痛。她反反复复在榻上辗转，想着她的孩子。
最后，她想下床去厨房，趁天还未明蒸屉馍馍。她撑着身体，一步步挪出房门，昏暗的夜色里，门槛隐去了身形。
于是，和锅碗陶盆一起摔碎的，还有阿婆的衰躯病体，和她最后的惦记和挂念。

王大犬总是在后悔。自己为什么要丢掉随信而来的馍呢。
他应该更懂事，多写些信，多寄些新鲜物什回家。可他没有，他只是一边奔波，一边丢掉了阿婆的馍。
如今，年年岁岁朔望依旧。而那个为他蒸馍馍的阿婆，早已化为月华，等待她的孩子捞起馍馍。
他知道，从此每一块吃到腹中的月光馍馍，都是阿婆对他的挂念，亦都是他对阿婆的亏欠。
en:
In all his years wandering, Wang Daquan often wrote home. Grandma's legs were weak, her eyesight poor—she relied on neighbors to read his letters. 
Occasionally, a reply would reach Wang Daquan. Opening it, he'd find only Grandma's ramblings—eat more, wear more. 
Grandma said she knew Daquan was a good boy, capable, diligent, and would take care of himself. 
With each letter came a small parcel containing Grandma's buns. Wang Daquan had written repeatedly that the journey was long, and the buns arrived hard and inedible. Yet, Grandma would steam fresh ones each time to send to her farthest child. 
Wang Daquan had no choice but to throw the rock-hard buns away. After all, south of the river was a land of plenty—what delicacies couldn't he find? 
Until the day an urgent letter arrived. 

Wang Daquan never knew that shortly after he left home, Grandma had fallen and injured her leg, confined to bed for months. 
Were it not for an aunt's care, Grandma might have starved. 
It was an ordinary night. Grandma couldn't sleep, her back burning with pain. Tossing and turning, she thought of her child. 
Finally, she decided to get up and steam a batch of buns before dawn. Leaning on furniture, she shuffled out of her room. In the dim light, the threshold was invisible. 
What shattered along with the pots and bowls was Grandma's frail body, and her final thoughts of worry and care. 

Wang Daquan was filled with regret. Why had he thrown away those buns? 
He should have been more understanding, written more letters, sent more fresh things home. But he hadn't. He had simply journeyed on, discarding Grandma's buns. 
Now, year after year, the moon waxes and wanes. The grandma who steamed buns for him has long since turned into moonlight, waiting for her child to scoop them up. 
He knows now that every moon-bun he eats is both Grandma's care for him and his own debt to her.

zh: 《尚书》成于先秦，乃上古史官记言记事之遗编，相传经孔子整理编次。全书分虞夏书、商书、周书三部，共五十八篇，以典、谟、训、诰、誓、命六体行文。所涉治国方略、君臣谋议、征战誓词、政令文告诸事，兼有地理、五行等专篇。秦火之后，汉伏生以隶书传今文二十八篇；东晋梅赜献古文五十八篇，流传既广，唐代定为官学取士之本。然梅赜所献古文，其间真伪，唐末五代学者已有议论。自汉以来，历代推为“政书之祖”，汉代儒家五经之一，是中国最早的历史文献汇编。
en: The Book of Documents was compiled before the Qin dynasty, and is a surviving record of words and deeds set down by the historians of high antiquity. It is said to have been arranged and edited by Confucius himself. The full work is divided into three parts: the Records of Yu and Xia, the Records of Shang, and the Records of Zhou, comprising fifty-eight pieces in total, written across six forms: Canon, Counsel, Instruction, Proclamation, Oath, and Command. Its subjects encompass statecraft, deliberations between ruler and minister, battle oaths, edicts and ordinances, as well as dedicated chapters on geography and the Five Phases. After the burning of books under the Qin, the Han scholar Fu Sheng transmitted twenty-eight chapters in clerical script as the New Text; in the Eastern Jin, Mei Ze presented fifty-eight chapters as the Old Text, which spread widely and was established in the Tang dynasty as the foundation of the official examinations. Yet the authenticity of the Old Text presented by Mei Ze had already been called into question by scholars of the late Tang and the Five Dynasties. From the Han onward, every age has extolled it as "the forefather of political writings." It stands among the Five Classics of Han Confucianism, and is the earliest compilation of historical documents in China.

zh: 钱江市井凌霄花浓，千家万户依水而生，多以商贾市易为业。每有货船归来，岸上购者熙攘，船不得行驶，遂约而为集，称花船集。 此处晨起开市，日暮而散，多售生活所需或手工活计。商贾以应季鲜花饰船揽客，争奇斗艳。人声鼎沸，舟楫相接，似水上花桥。
en: In the Qianjiang Streets, the trumpet flowers bloom thick and heavy, and countless households live along the water, most making their living through trade and commerce. Whenever cargo boats return, buyers throng the shore so densely that the boats can scarcely move, and so, by common accord, a market formed here—known as the Flower Boat Market. This place opens for business at dawn and disperses at dusk, selling mostly daily necessities and handcrafted goods. Merchants deck their boats with seasonal flowers to draw in customers, each vying to outshine the other in splendor. Amid the clamor of voices and the press of boat against boat, it seems almost a bridge of flowers rising from the water.

zh:
【季氏第十六】

季氏将伐颛臾。冉有、季路见于孔子曰：“季氏将有事于颛臾。”孔子曰：“求，无乃尔是过与？夫颛臾，昔者先王以为东蒙主，且在邦域之中矣，是社稷之臣也，何以为伐也？。”冉有曰：“夫子欲之，吾二臣者皆不欲也。”孔子曰：“求！周任有言曰：‘陈力就列，不能者止。’危而不持，颠而不扶，则将焉用彼相矣？且尔言过矣，虎兕出于柙，龟玉毁椟中，是谁之过与？”冉有曰：“今夫颛臾，固而近于费，今不取，后世必为子孙忧。”孔子曰：“求！君子疾夫舍曰欲之而必更为之辞。丘也闻有国有家者，不患寡而患不均，不患贫而患不安。盖均无贫，和无寡，安无倾。夫如是，故远人不服，则修文德以来之，既来之，则安之。今由与求也，相夫子，远人不服而不能来也，邦分崩离折而不能守也，而谋动干戈于邦内，吾恐季孙之忧，不在于颛臾，而在萧墙之内也。”
孔子曰：“天下有道，则礼乐征伐自天子出。天下无道，则礼乐征伐自诸侯出。自诸侯出，盖十世希不失矣。自大夫出，五世希不失矣。陪臣执国命，三世希不失矣。天下有道，则政不在大夫。天下有道，则庶人不议。”
孔子曰：“禄之去公室五世矣。政逮大夫，四世矣。故夫三桓之子孙微矣。”
孔子曰：“益者三友，损者三友。友直，友谅，友多闻，益矣。友便僻，友善柔，友便佞，损矣。”
孔子曰：“益者三乐，损者三乐。乐节礼乐，乐道人之善，乐多贤友，益矣。乐骄乐，乐佚游，乐宴乐，损矣。”
孔子曰：“侍于君子有三愆：言未及之而言，谓之躁。言及之不言，谓之隐。未见颜色而言，谓之瞽。”
孔子曰：“君子有三戒：少之时，血气未定，戒之在色。及其壮也，血气方刚，戒之在斗。及其老也，血气既衰，戒之在得。”
孔子曰：“君子有三畏：畏天命，畏大人，畏圣人之言。小人不知天命而不畏也，狎大人，侮圣人之言。”
孔子曰：“生而知之者，上也。学而知之者，次也。困而学之，又其次也；困而不学，民斯为下矣。”
孔子曰：“君子有九思：视思明，听思聪，色思温，貌思恭，言思忠，事思敬，疑思问，忿思难，见得思义。”
……
en:
Book 16: Ji Shi

The Ji family was about to attack Zhuanyu. Ran You and Ji Lu went to see Confucius and said, "The Ji family is going to take action against Zhuanyu." Confucius said, "Qiu, is this not your fault? In the past, the former kings made the lord of Zhuanyu the master of Dongmeng, and it is within the borders of the state. It is a minister of the state, so why attack it?" Ran You said, "Our master wants to do it; we two ministers do not." Confucius said, "Qiu! Zhou Ren has a saying: 'If you can fulfill your duties, take your place; if you cannot, step down.' If you do not support when in danger, nor assist when falling, then what use are you as ministers? Moreover, what you say is wrong. If a tiger or rhinoceros escapes from its cage, or if a tortoise-shell or jade is broken in its casket, whose fault is it?" Ran You said, "Now Zhuanyu is strong and close to Bi. If we do not take it now, future generations will surely worry about it for their descendants." Confucius said, "Qiu! A gentleman hates those who, instead of saying they desire something, make excuses for it. I have heard that those who have states or families do not worry about poverty but about inequality, not worry about scarcity but about instability. For if there is equality, there is no poverty; if there is harmony, there is no scarcity; if there is stability, there is no collapse. Thus, if distant people do not submit, cultivate culture and virtue to attract them. Once they come, make them content. Now, you and Qiu assist your master, yet distant people do not submit and you cannot attract them; the state is divided and collapsing, and you cannot preserve it. Instead, you plan to wage war within the state. I fear that the worry of Ji Sun lies not in Zhuanyu but within his own walls."
Confucius said, "When the Way prevails under Heaven, rites, music, and punitive expeditions come from the Son of Heaven. When the Way is lost under Heaven, rites, music, and punitive expeditions come from the feudal lords. When they come from the feudal lords, it is rare for the state to last ten generations. When they come from the ministers, it is rare for it to last five generations. When the stewards hold the state's command, it is rare for it to last three generations. When the Way prevails under Heaven, governance does not rest with the ministers. When the Way prevails under Heaven, the common people do not criticize."
Confucius said, "The emoluments have left the ducal house for five generations. Governance has fallen to the ministers for four generations. Therefore, the descendants of the three Huan families are in decline."
Confucius said, "There are three types of beneficial friends and three types of harmful friends. To befriend the upright, the sincere, and the knowledgeable is beneficial. To befriend the flattering, the insincere, and the glib is harmful."
Confucius said, "There are three types of beneficial pleasures and three types of harmful pleasures. To take pleasure in the moderation of rites and music, in speaking of others' virtues, and in having many worthy friends is beneficial. To take pleasure in arrogance, in idleness, and in feasting is harmful."
Confucius said, "There are three faults in serving a gentleman: speaking when it is not your turn is called rashness; not speaking when it is your turn is called concealment; speaking without observing the countenance is called blindness."
Confucius said, "A gentleman has three things to guard against: in youth, when the blood and vital energy are not yet settled, guard against lust; in maturity, when the blood and vital energy are at their peak, guard against strife; in old age, when the blood and vital energy have declined, guard against greed."
Confucius said, "A gentleman has three things to fear: he fears the Mandate of Heaven, he fears great men, and he fears the words of the sages. A petty man does not know the Mandate of Heaven and does not fear it; he is disrespectful to great men and mocks the words of the sages."
Confucius said, "Those who are born with knowledge are the highest. Those who learn and acquire knowledge are next. Those who learn through hardship are next again. Those who face hardship but do not learn are the lowest among the people."
Confucius said, "A gentleman has nine things to consider: in seeing, consider clarity; in hearing, consider acuity; in expression, consider warmth; in demeanor, consider respectfulness; in speech, consider loyalty; in service, consider reverence; in doubt, consider inquiry; in anger, consider the difficulties; in gain, consider righteousness."

少东家：

哥这趟出门，大大小小的新鲜事可没少听。昨儿在驿站的茶舍里，哥还偷听到邻桌茶客说他邻居，因为跟老婆吵架，一怒之下，挥刀自宫了……

可见这天之大，正常的人和狗装不下，这才造出来了奇葩。

本来哥攒了满肚子八卦，就等着回去后，跟你叨叨着下酒……可这狗生奇缘就这么悄没声地来了。

昨儿路过飞花渡的画舫，隔着人堆里飘过来一阵琵琶调，唰一下，直接把哥的魂儿勾走了。不夸张，狗生十年可没听过这么带劲儿的小调！

哥那小心脏呦……扑通扑通的，摁都摁不住。

说到这儿，少东家，你肯定也猜到了，哥这信是来请辞的。

半路撂挑子确实不地道，哥懂，可你也常说“大侠处事，当断则断”。狗生第二春摆在眼前，家里这摊活，哥只能先往后搁一搁了……

但你放心，哥可不是那等甩手掌柜，等哥追着了爱情，必定夫妻双双把家还，她弹曲儿来我刨洞，一块儿把你那小家经营得和和美美的。

你最靠谱的伏禄娃留



（信笺附言： 那弹琵琶的姑娘，哥打听了，好像还是个梨园的名角，叫什么、什么万春姑娘的，害羞得紧，至今连面也不愿露。哥预备着先混进他们排演的后院。近水楼台，不怕追不着！）
en:
Woof woof, woof... woof woof!!!
Young Master:
I've heard plenty of wild tales on this trip. Yesterday, at a teahouse in courier station, I overheard a guy at the next table saying his neighbor got into a fight with his wife and castrated himself in a fit of rage...
It just goes to show, the world is too big for only normal people and dogs; that's why weirdos exist.
I had a belly full of gossip, waiting to chat with you over drinks when I got back... but then, my romantic destiny arrived out of nowhere.
Yesterday, walking past the painted boats at Petalfall Crossing, a pipa tune drifted through the crowd and snatched my soul right away. I'm not exaggerating—in ten years of my dog life, I've never heard a tune with such a kick!
My little heart... thump, thump, thump, I just couldn't calm it down.
Speaking of this, Young Master, you must have guessed it. This letter is my resignation.
Quitting halfway isn't cool, I know. But you always say, "A hero acts decisively." With my second spring of love right in front of me, the work back home has to take a backseat...
But don't worry, I won't just vanish. Once I catch my true love, we'll return home together. She plays the tunes, I dig the holes, and we'll run that little household of yours beautifully.
Your most reliable Fu Luwa
(P.S.: I asked around about the girl playing the pipa. Seems she's a famous performer from The Masked Troupe, Lady Wanchun or something. She's very shy and hasn't even shown her face yet. I plan to sneak into their rehearsal backyard first. A little proximity works wonders!)

zh:
那婴孩发出鸣啼之时，正是秦王身死之际。
李筠知斯人已逝，于是毅然转身，带着那婴孩遁走北境。

这一生长路漫漫，而被他赐名“鸢”的孩子，蹦蹦跳跳，能说会笑，是独属于他的慰藉。
但那孩子逐年长大，而他颠沛多年，居无定所。
他得做出选择。一些正确的选择。替自己，也替那孩子。
慕容世代将门，家族煊赫，为人淳厚。
会是那孩子很好的归所。

李筠拄着银枪，半身已染风雪。
不远处，那孩子发出鸣啼。
而他毅然转身，恰如多年前的那个晚上。
长路漫漫，李筠心想，只愿这漫天风雪，全由他一人承担。
en:
The child's first cry rang out at the very moment King Qin drew his final breath. 
Li Jun knew the man was gone. Without hesitation, he turned and fled north, the infant swaddled in his arms. 

It was a long, uncertain road. But the child he named Yuan was lively, cheerful, full of chatter, she became a joy that belonged to him and him alone. 
But as the child grew older, Li Jun had wandered the land for far too long. He had no home, no rest. 
He had to make a choice. The right choice. For himself, and for the child. 
The Murong family, born of generals, steeped in honor, upright in heart. 
It would be a good place for the child to belong. 

Leaning on his silver spear, his body half-covered in frost and snow. 
The child cried again, not far behind. 
Once more, he turned away. Just like he had on that distant night, years ago. 
The road ahead is long. And if storms were to come, let them fall upon him alone.
MadaraThorn

青州海上，传说纷纭，有宝船者，首雕胖鱼，身耀龙鳞，船头指处，便是蓬莱仙山。山在虚无缥缈间，见过的人再未归来，未归的人成为新的传说，在一代代舟师口中相传。
适逢雨季，沈溺者众。沿海径海岸边，有女孩徘徊不去，等舟楫归航，引溺者上岸。此时前往，或可听她讲一段八仙过海的故事。。
en:
"Sea mist rises thick, conjuring towering pavilions. A fabled treasure ship sails the northern and southern seas. Ride it on the great winds to Penglai, then east to where the sun rises, to rest among the sacred branches."

The seas off Qingzhou are rich with legend. One tells of a treasure ship with a plump fish carved on its prow and dragon scales gleaming along its hull. Wherever its prow points lies Mount Penglai. Hidden in a realm beyond the mortal world, it is said that none who find the mountain ever return. Those who do not come back become new legends, passed from sailor to sailor through the generations.
Now that the rainy season is here, many are lost to the sea. Along the shore by Cliffside Path, a girl lingers, waiting for the boats to return and helping pull the drowning ashore. Go to her now, and you may hear a tale of the Eight Immortals crossing the sea.

zh: 陛下需要什么，这世上就有什么。 陛下需要什么样的人，这世上就有什么样的人。 一个为他奔走，联络各方的人。 一个熟悉突厥对胜利的渴望，公主的骄横，江湖高僧的隐秘苦痛，以及道真掌教那颗圣人心上轻微裂痕的人。  慕容晚就是这样的人。他自得于自己江湖名门的出身，自信于朝堂风云的掌控，从此名门变朱门。 最后他成功了，至少在他活的时候。 只是这朝堂得意安长久？朱门换匾如转头。 后代如何，是另一个故事了。
en: The world bends to the Emperor's will. Whatever he desires, the realm provides. Whomever he requires, the realm produces. He required a shadow to bridge the empire's fractured powers. He needed someone who intimately understood the ravenous Turkic hunger for conquest, the Princess's blinding vanity, the buried agonies of the jianghu monk, and that single, hairline fracture across the saintly heart of the Daozhen patriarch. Murong Wan was exactly that man. Supremely proud of his roots in an illustrious martial clan, yet dangerously confident in his ability to navigate the treacherous storms of the royal court, he eagerly traded the austere honor of the jianghu for the painted crimson doors of the high aristocracy. He succeeded, of course, at least for the span of his own life. But how long does courtly triumph ever truly last? The gilded name plaques above noble estates change hands in the blink of an eye. As for what became of his lineage... that is a story for another time.

Lie Yan, one of the Eight Talents of Hedong, possessed a body of iron and a spirit to match. His rare words carried weight, embodying the same righteousness that made Lord Guan legendary. Though short in stature, his ambition towered like a mountain. After the battle at Yannan Gate, he vanished from the jianghu without a trace.
Rumors of sightings near Qinghe led me into the mists of Sundara Land. A hundred steps west lies General's Shrine. A thousand kowtows, and the truth is revealed. This place holds lingering regret—only those with sincere hearts will receive his guidance.

论剑玩法中有特殊的战斗规则。

论剑中释放卸势会消耗耐力，而处决命中时会回复耐力。

玩家的技能大多都可以以卸势应对，破防奇术不仅不会被卸势，在命中处于防御或在释放卸势技能的目标时，反而有更好的效果，但其可以被任意技能打断。

玩家的各类技能（包括奇术和蓄力技）能够打断轻重击，而反过来则不行。

活用解控技能可以有效扭转劣势。

战胜你的对手可获取论剑积分，积分高的大侠将进入排行榜。

论剑玩法中，玩家造成的治疗效果降低90%。对目标的气血护盾，造成的伤害提升100%。

论剑玩法中闪避的不可选中时长增幅百分比上限为20%

在限定时间内，率先击败对方的一方获胜，若倒计时结束未分胜负，按以下优先级依次判定：
1.存活玩家数量更多的一方获胜；
2.若存活玩家数量相同，则总伤害量更高一方获胜；
3.若总伤害量相同，则总治疗量更高一方获胜。
en:
Special combat rules apply in the 1v1 Arena mode. 

Using Deflect consumes Endurance, while finishing Execute restores Endurance. 

Most player skills can be deflected. Defense-breaking Mystic Skills not only ignore deflect but also deal enhanced effects when hitting targets who are defending or deflecting. However, these Mystic Skills can be interrupted by any skill. 

Player skills, including Mystic Skills and Charged Skill, can interrupt Light and Heavy Attacks, but not vice versa. 

Effective use of Control-breaking Skills can turn the tide. 

Defeating your rival grants 1v1 Arena Points. Heroes with the higher points will enter the Arena Leaderboard. 

In 1v1 Arena, player Healing effects are reduced by 90%; Damage to targets' HP Shields is increased by 100%.

In 1v1 Arena, the maximum increase percentage for the untargetable duration of Dodge is capped at 20%.

The side that defeats the other first within the time limit wins. If the timer runs out without a decisive outcome, the winner is determined by the following priorities:
1. The side with more surviving players wins;
2. If the number of surviving players is equal, the side with the higher total damage dealt wins;
3. If the total damage dealt is equal, the side with the higher total healing amount wins.

zh:
它不是它爹亲生的狗，而是捡回来的一只小崽。
也许是因为这，它从吃奶的时候，就会打架了。
别的狗都说，将来的头领多半就是这崽儿了。

它才不想当头领嘞，它就喜欢打架。
不是为了地盘，也不是为了骨头，就是喜欢打赢了汪汪汪的感觉！
虽然偶尔也输。
一开始，打了一身伤回来，也不吭声，自己舔干净。
后来它越来越厉害，输的少了，有时候回来，别的狗还能看到它身上有人帮忙包扎的痕迹。
也是，毕竟阿崽在狗里，也是个靓崽。

这些，头领狗都看在眼里。

唯一一次，头领狗当着一窝狗教训阿崽，
是因为阿崽学头领的样子，去偷喝人类的酒。
它喝得东倒西歪，被叼回窝里，头领狗黑着脸吼它又让它一个月不准吃骨头。
第二天，别的狗七嘴八舌地汪。告诉阿崽，它醉了的时候，叫头领狗了一声——爹。
阿崽的耳朵往后趴了趴，假装没听见，甩甩尾巴，又出门打架去了。

那时它还以为，
这样的日子能过很久很久——
打完架，照旧能顺着味道，摸回家
在头领狗的草垫旁，睡一觉，做个小崽子。
en:
He isn't Alpha's biological son, but a stray rescued as a pup.
Perhaps because of this, he's been fighting ever since he was nursing.
The other dogs say he'll likely be the next leader.

He doesn't want to be leader; he just loves fighting.
Not for territory or bones, just for that "woof-woof-woof" feeling of winning!
Though occasionally, he loses.
At first, he'd return covered in wounds, saying nothing and licking them clean himself.
Later, he grew stronger and lost less often. Sometimes when he returned, the other dogs could see bandages wrapped by humans.
True, because Pup is quite a handsome fellow, even among dogs.

Alpha saw all of this.

The only time Alpha scolded Pup in front of the whole pack,
Was when Pup imitated Alpha and stole some human wine.
He stumbled around drunk until he was carried back to the nest. Alpha growled with a dark face and banned him from eating bones for a month.
The next day, the other dogs barked all at once, telling Pup that when he was drunk, he had called Alpha: "Dad."
Pup flattened his ears, pretending not to hear, wagged his tail, and went out to fight again.

Back then, he thought,
Those days would last forever...
He could always follow the scent home after a fight,
And sleep beside Alpha's grass mat, being a little pup again.
Miles Within Inches
I've come here to reflect on history.

zh:
我这辈子，也算是该吃的都吃了，该玩的都玩了，该见的都见了。但每每想到那个遥远的雨夜，那个跌落在河水中的奇怪女人……就觉得，我还是见识少了。

那夜，我正在凿山采玉，忽然间风雨大作，正欲寻一处山洞避雨时，一道惊雷轰然炸开，我悬挂的绳子断裂，我就要坠到那崖底去。
我死死抓住了山石，此刻第二道雷响了，我想要张望存身之机，此时看见——那个奇怪女人就这么被惊雷裹挟着， 跌跌撞撞走入黑沉沉的水中。
她身材修长，并不娇小，可此刻蜷缩着身体，远远望去，竟像是被抛入水中的弃婴。
我不记得有没有听到她的呜咽声，只记得她垂头沉默了半晌，忽地仰起头来，对着漆黑的夜空厉声发问：屈原大夫！当年你报国无门纵身投江之时，也曾作过这样一场穷途之哭吗？！

回答她的只有风雨。

她似乎泄了气，慢慢地沉下身子，任凭水面没过自己。彻底地没过。
可是，就在我以为她要消失在水下时——四周忽然风声大作，虚影憧憧，像是无数魂灵，穿越洪荒宇宙，发出声声长啸。

“胭脂裂作甲光寒，玉门雪淬剑眉丹！”风声有如人语，像是在催促她起身。
“莫道红颜非铁甲，巾帼何曾让须眉！”她的声音从水下传来，似是回应。

一道闪电撕开天幕，刹那间，四周亮如白昼——一个人猛地从水中站起身来，拖着长长的龙尾，在风声中，在长啸里。
我认出她来了！她是那位大唐的公主！

我明白了！我全明白了！方才那一声声将她唤出黑水的长啸，定然属于雪夜出塞的王昭君，驱驰千里的刘解忧，玉门叩雪的文成公主……属于无数个远嫁番邦的薄命金枝。

风声呼啸，天门中开，暴雨如注，倾泻而下。被史官笔墨吞没的声响，此刻全成了刺向苍穹的刃鸣。
是无数个公主托举着她浮出了水面，亦是她牵引着无数个公主，要登九天之门。

她带着一群人的殷殷期盼，纵身一跃，完成这一场化龙之变；
她们也在她弓身迎击雷暴时，化成她脊背上坚硬的鳞片！
亦或，那从水里浮起来的，真的是她，而不是她们吗？

她们一起往高处走，往穷途走，走回来处，去向苍穹。在如注的暴雨中，迎向万钧雷霆。

她们走了。
在这样的雷霆与暴雨中，我早已分不清自己看到了什么，听到了什么。
我所感受到的，只是对公主们的同情、怜惜或者赞美吗？
不，我感受到的是自己汩汩流动的血，回荡胸间的气——我又生出无数的力气，拽紧凸起的石头，我要攀上那高高的悬崖，我要活下去。
我要去读书，我要写诗，我要把我看到的记下来——让现在读这本书的你看到。
我不知道我将何时死去，但终究，我没有死在那天的断崖之下。她也没有。
en:
In my life, I've eaten all I wanted, played all I wanted, and seen all I wanted. But whenever I think of that distant rainy night, that strange woman who fell into the river... I feel I still haven't seen enough. 

That night, I was chiseling jade from the mountain. Suddenly, a violent storm erupted. As I was about to find a cave to take shelter, a thunderbolt crashed, my hanging rope snapped, and I was about to fall to the cliff bottom. 
I clung tightly to the rock. Just then, a second thunderbolt struck. As I searched for a way to survive, I saw her, that strange woman, swept up by the thunderbolt, stumbling into the dark, churning water. 
She was tall and slender, not petite. But curled up like that, from a distance, she looked like an abandoned baby thrown into the water. 
I don't remember if I heard her sobs, only that she bowed her head in silence for a while, then suddenly lifted her face and shouted fiercely at the dark night sky, "Master Qu Yuan! When you threw yourself into the river, having no way to serve your country, did you also utter such a cry of utter despair?" 

Only wind and rain answered her. 

She seemed deflated, slowly sinking, letting the water surface cover her. Completely cover her. 
But just when I thought she would vanish beneath the water, suddenly, wind howled all around, phantom shadows flickered, as if countless souls traversed primordial cosmos, emitting long cries. 

"Rouge cracks into cold armor light, Jade Gate snow tempers sword-brows crimson!" The wind sounded like human speech, as if urging her to rise. 
"Say not that rosy cheeks are not iron armor, when have heroines ever yielded to men?" Her voice came from underwater, as if in response. 

A lightning bolt tore the sky. In an instant, all around became bright as day, a person stood up abruptly from the water, dragging a long dragon tail, amidst the howling wind and long cries. 
I recognized her! She was that Tang princess! 

I understand! I fully understand! Those cries that summoned her from the black waters just now must belong to Wang Zhaojun venturing beyond the frontier on a snowy night, Liu Jieyou galloping a thousand miles, Princess Wencheng knocking on Yumen's snow... belong to countless ill-fated noble daughters married far to foreign lands. 

Wind howled, the heavenly gate opened wide, torrential rain poured down. Sounds swallowed by historians' ink now all became blade-songs piercing the firmament. 
Countless princesses lifted her out of the water; and she led countless princesses, striving to climb the gate to heaven. 

Carrying the earnest hopes of a multitude, she leaped, completing this transformation into a dragon. 
And as she bowed to face the thunderstorm, they transformed into the hard scales on her back. 
Or was it really her who emerged from the water, or them? 

Together, they walked upward, toward the end of the road, returning to their origin, ascending to the sky. Amidst the torrential rain, they faced the overwhelming thunder. 

They left. 
Amidst such thunder and rain, I could no longer tell what I had seen or heard. 
What I felt, was it merely sympathy, pity, or praise for the princesses? 
No, I felt the blood flowing in my veins, the power surging in my chest. I suddenly regained immense strength, gripping the protruding rocks tightly. I would climb that high cliff. I would survive. 
I would go study, I would write poetry, I would record what I saw, so that you who read this book now may see. 
I do not know when I will die, but in the end, I did not die beneath that day's broken cliff. Nor did she.

zh:
广顺二年，清河有隐名藏姓者，捐金三百两于文津馆。
此人信中自言：少时失怙，飘零江湖，幸遇女侠援手，方见天光。今结为伉俪，琴瑟和鸣。其妻良善，故他欲近善、行善，以赎经年之憾、难言之罪。
然自省平生，身无长物，连一衣一履，皆非己有——唯此三百金，一瓢一笠自力所得，锱铢无垢，可助他人。
余遂收此金于馆中，遂其愿，专助孤童求学，此亦是其人之妻之愿也。
首受其惠者，任灰姑。北地流民，颖悟非常而家徒四壁。彼时稚子尚幼，于饱腹与读书之间，踌躇难决。恰此金至天光破云，遂得入文津馆，因缘际会拜于余门下。
今习学月余，《千字文》已诵如流，自取大名“任非相”。
人惑何不取《楚辞》香草？
正色对曰：“诸相非相，皆因缘幻化。吾欲为江湖史笔，书尽虚实之相耳！”
童言近道，妙哉！妙哉！
然近来，余徒于择史本经，抑或法本经之处渐生迷惘。余观之甚慰，余徒昔年于饥寒间无可抉之，今有余裕择道，此幸事也。
万事答案，皆出于实地践行。余谓其亲往胜乐门一行，修史载事毕，或可知心之所求。
前尘玄妙，还望吾徒此行平安，得遂其愿，切盼得归！
en:
In the second year of Guangshun, an anonymous benefactor in Qinghe donated three hundred taels of gold to the Inkbound Order. In his letter, the man stated that he had lost his parents in his youth and wandered the martial world alone, until he was fortunate enough to be saved by a righteous swordswoman, finally seeing the light of day. Now united as husband and wife, they live in perfect harmony. His wife possesses a kind heart; thus, he wishes to embrace and practice kindness, hoping to atone for the regrets and unspeakable sins of his past years. However, upon reflecting on his life, he realized he owned nothing of value. Even his clothes and shoes were not truly his. Only these three hundred taels of gold, earned through solitary toil with naught but a begging bowl and a woven hat, remained utterly pure and untainted, fit to aid others. I therefore accepted this gold into the Order to fulfill his wish, dedicating it entirely to the education of orphaned children, which was also the heartfelt desire of his wife.
The first to receive this grace was Ren Huigu. She was a refugee from the north, exceptionally brilliant yet entirely destitute. At that time, still a young child, she hesitated bitterly between filling her stomach and pursuing studies. The arrival of this gold was like sunlight piercing through the clouds. She was admitted into the Inkbound Order and, by karmic destiny, became a disciple under my tutelage.
Now, having studied for over a month, she recites the Thousand-Character Classic with absolute fluency and has chosen a formal name for herself: Ren Feixiang. People were puzzled, asking why she did not choose a name from the fragrant herbs in the Songs of Chu. She replied with a solemn face, "All appearances are but non-forms, born of fleeting karmic conditions. I wish to wield the historian's brush for the martial world, recording the ultimate truth and falsehood of all forms!" For a child's words to resonate so closely with the Great Way is truly marvelous!
Recently, however, my disciple has grown perplexed when choosing between the study of historical annals and martial scriptures. Observing this, I feel deeply comforted. In the past, amidst hunger and cold, she had no choices to make; today, she has the luxury to choose her path, and that is a profound blessing. The answers to all things in the world emerge solely from practical experience. I advised her to travel to the Shengle Sect in person. Once her historical records of the events there are complete, she might discover what her heart truly seeks.
The past remains deeply mysterious. I only hope my disciple stays safe on this journey, fulfills her wishes, and returns to me soon!

褚清泉自知命不久矣，有些话他只得嘱托给伊刀：一是要去神仙渡问出江无浪的秘密，二是秘密事关大计，而大计未成自己放心不下，三是香寻……。话还未说完，就听得伊刀斥他这人屁话忒多，自己可不会给他跑腿，倒不如闭嘴省些力气。褚清泉还真听起话来，阖上双眼不再开口。二人沉默了一路，直到耳边忽现水声。离得近了，水声更大，似有猛兽出笼，奔涌向南。伊刀紧了紧绳子，只道了句：“该渡河了。”

话音很快就被水声掩过，也不知褚清泉究竟听没听到。若他听到了，可会想起从前千里孤行，渡河北上？而如今，明月千里，再难渡河。
en:
Chu Qingquan knew his time was short. There were things he had to entrust to Yi Dao:First, to go to Heaven's Pier and uncover the truth behind Jiang Wulang. Second, that this secret was part of a far greater plan, one that remained unfinished and weighed on his soul. And third was Xiangxun... Before he could finish, Yi Dao cut him off, complaining about Chu's ranting and how he was not his errand boy. Surprisingly, Chu Qingquan obeyed. He closed his eyes and said nothing more. The two continued in silence, until the sound of rushing water filled the air. As they drew closer, the river roared like a caged beast breaking free, surging southward. Yi Dao tightened the rope. "Time to cross." 

His words were drowned almost instantly by the torrent.
Whether Chu Qingquan heard him or not, no one could say. If he had, perhaps he would've remembered that long journey north, crossing rivers alone beneath a distant moon. But now, though the moon was still high in the sky, the river could no longer be crossed.

zh:
他太饿了，闻着香味去了码头那宴席，席上有人做鱼，还有人做面，那碧绿色的面，他从来没有见过，香得他走进了火里都不知道，直到一群人喊着他听不懂的话过来，他知道这些人，别人把他们叫做契丹人。
  他吓得不敢动，缩在角落，最后偷到的半块馍馍掉在地上，他想去捡，又不敢去，那块馍馍在人群中被踢来踢去，他的眼睛跟着馍馍动。
  他看见一位中年男子和一位年轻男人踢了他的馍馍第一脚，他们手忙脚乱地将一个女人锁进屋子中，那女人嗓门大得很，力气也大，那馍馍被踢得远远的。
  第二个踢到他馍馍的是那做面的厨子，她四处看，大声喊着树生，像是在找什么人，那眼神就像是他看着馍馍一样，那馍馍是他最宝贵的东西。
  然后那馍馍滚到一个姑娘脚下，她挡在一位被吓坏了的妇人面前，然后血溅在馍馍上，白馍馍变成了红馍馍。
  那红馍馍滚啊滚，滚到了三具尸体身下，一对爹娘带着一个姑娘，那姑娘尸体下压着一盒小小的崭新的灯油。
  他想要去追那半块馍馍，没人能看见他吧，没人能看见他吧，他这样想着，追着那半块馍馍去了，他伸手向着那块馍馍的时候，那契丹人的刀举在他的头顶上，那半块红馍馍被契丹人一脚踢开，滚下了码头，滚进了河里，他想自己这辈子都吃不上馍馍了。
en:
Starving, he followed the irresistible aroma to the dock—where Khitans were cooking fish and noodles.
Terrified, he froze in a corner as the half piece of stolen bun slipped from his hand and was kicked around by the crowd. His eyes never left it.
A middle-aged man and a younger one kicked it first. The noodle cook followed, calling desperately, her eyes as desperate as his own for that precious bun.
The bun rolled to a girl shielding a frightened woman, and then blood spattered onto it. It came to stop beneath three dead bodies—a mother, father, and daughter—with a new box of lamp oil beneath the girl.
He tried to retrieve the bun, hoping no one would see, but a Khitan's blade rose above him, and the soldier kicked the bloodied bun off the dock into the river. In that moment, he knew he might never eat buns again.

伏火硫磺，形细末，色黄褐。需以北亭砂、硫磺二味经研末、封存、晒干、火煅而成。然二者孰几，尚无定论。今乃分第等，多回试之，所见所察，记述如下。
初试
#F硫磺一，北亭砂三#E，去砂石，研为末。文火煅之，烟雾逸之。候烟雾沉尽，取出，见灰土结于其中，色灰白。#F错。#E
再试
#F硫磺三，北亭砂一#E，去砂石，研为末。文火煅之，见烟少许。取出，得黄粉，捻之，如顽卤。#F错。#E
三试
硫磺四，北亭砂五，研为末，力竭……错。
四试
硫磺八，研为末，误吸，昏厥……错。
五试
错！错！错！
……
二十三试
硫磺三，北亭砂四，文火炒之，见烟少许，加粟米一，蜂蜜二分，香味逸之。弃粉末，食粟米……错。
三十四试
冯继升啊冯继升！区区三十几次失败，怎么就将你打败了！提振精神，继续实验！
三十五试
#F硫磺二，北亭砂二#E，去砂石，研为末，择#F木炭#E为薪，大火爆炒！
烟雾逸之，添木炭，大火爆炒！
火力渐盛，添木炭，大火爆炒！
……
续：炉骤裂，声如雷，黑烟四溢，结灰于冯师兄面上，色漆黑。
劝告后来者，#F慎大火爆炒。#E——小磊
en:
Processed sulfur: fine powder, yellow-brown.
Made from sulfur and Beiting Sand. Grind, seal, sun-dry, then calcine. Exact ratios unknown. Ran multiple trials. Notes below.

Initial test: #F1 part sulfur, 3 parts Beiting Sand#E
Removed grit. Ground to powder. Low heat calcination. Smoke throughout.
When the smoke cleared, retrieved the batch. Gray-white ash clumped inside.
#FWrong.#E

Second test: #F3 parts sulfur, 1 part Beiting Sand#E
Removed grit. Ground to powder. Low heat calcination. Very little smoke.
Retrieved. Yellow powder. Rubbed between fingers, it cakes into hard lumps.
#FWrong.#E

Third test: 4 parts sulfur, 5 parts Beiting Sand. Ground until I could not feel my arms...
Wrong.

Fourth test: 8 parts sulfur. Ground. Inhaled some by mistake. Passed out...
Wrong.

Fifth test: WRONG! WRONG! WRONG!
...

23rd test: 3 parts sulfur, 4 parts Beiting Sand. Low heat roast. A little smoke.
Added 1 part millet, 0.2 parts honey. Smelled amazing.
Dumped the powder. Ate the millet...
Wrong.

34th test:
Feng Jisheng, Feng Jisheng! It was only thirty-some failures. How did that break you?
Get it together. Keep testing!

35th test: #F2 parts sulfur, 2 parts Beiting Sand#E
Removed grit. Ground to powder. Used #FCharcoal#E as fuel.
Blazing heat, hard roast! Smoke surged. Added more charcoal. Blazing heat, hard roast!
Heat climbed. Added more charcoal. Blazing heat, hard roast!
...

Addendum: The furnace cracked with a bang, loud as thunder. Thick black smoke filled the room.
Soot caked Senior Brother Feng's face, pitch-black.

To whoever comes after: #FDo not crank the heat up like this.#E
Lei

en:
Granny Turtle checked her Treasure Basin once again. Lately, a lot more coins have appeared inside it.
She asked around, and people told her they were Song Coins.
Oh... then these are good coins. With Song Coins, she could buy Yingying a new pair of shoes. The girl ran and skipped everywhere, and her shoes were all worn through... She could save a little for the eldest, too. No, no, the eldest hadn't come home yet, but the youngest had.
The youngest was a good child, always coming and going in a whirlwind. When that fierce-looking man barged in, it was the youngest who stood right in front of her and Yingying.
Granny Turtle calculated in her head. The coins from the Treasure Basin, these Song Coins, could buy so many things: flatbreads, steamed buns, rolls, noodles... The youngest would never have to live on thin gruel again. Ah, yes, the wheat had been harvested too. She should save a little toward buying land for both Yingying and the youngest.
But she couldn't just save it all. If the youngest came back, she ought to buy...

Now, hearing that the battle at Zhongdu Bridge is about to start, he's found exactly what he's been looking for! He rushed all the way here, not for money or fame, but just to sharpen his blade, which hasn't tasted blood in far too long.

zh:
文津馆藏书万轴间，多有秘辛。有书云：观色辨象，下士视朱紫，不过十种；上智察秋毫，可辨百彩。林籁发响，庸者闻数鸟啁啾，达者识百禽宫商。武道之中，有可听声辨位，闻风知变者，其天授异秉，盖因灵“窍”通明，能察万物未涌之息。
先贤有云，人，乃天地之窍，亦自成一体。察百籁声场，与之谐振。师旷辨音识，离娄望气，自古有之。又有言，天地众窍，奇窍者多也，非人独属。 更有“事涉虚诞，未见其实”云云。 不可定论。
en:
The Inkbound Order once held a sea of books, and among them were hidden secrets. One claimed that the mediocre eye sees only a few loud colors, while the rare mind can separate a hundred hues from a single sunset. One hears birdsong; another hears structure, rhythm, intention. In the martial world, there are those who can locate an enemy by the tremor in a breath, and sense change in the wind. Some call it talent. Some call it destiny.
The old masters spoke instead of opened apertures, a clarity within that resonates with the pulse of heaven and earth. They said a person is not merely flesh, but a listening point in the great field of sound and light. History remembers men who could hear law in chaos and read omens in color. Others dismiss such stories as embellishment. Perhaps they are. Yet the idea persists that beyond ordinary sight and hearing lies a deeper current, waiting for someone capable of tuning in.

en: The ancients, too, had a deep reverence for relics of the past. When the poet Du Mu wrote of "a broken halberd buried in the sand, its iron not yet rusted away," he was surely stirred by the sight of some forgotten battlefield ruin. They demand to know exactly which dynasty forged them, whose hands carved the text, and from what earth they were drawn. Nor do they measure an object's worth by its sheer size or grandeur. A massive bronze cauldron, standing several feet high, might be nothing more than a mundane vessel. The yellow croaker of Luokou is said to be without equal.

Its flavor is famed for its delicacy, inspiring the saying: "Of all fish in the world, Luokou's yellow croaker stands above."

zh:
1. 等级突破
满足突破条件，即可进行等级突破，#H每次突破后均可获得一份珍贵的奖励#E。

2. 等级影响
随着单人模式等级提升，#H角色等级上限也会提升#E。相应的，大世界中的部分区域等级会提升从而导致敌人变得更强，但同时获得的奖励也会提升，包括：#H野兽、野外及据点中的敌人强度与击败奖励#E。

3. 等级调整
支持对模式等级进行调整。包括等级回退和恢复，会相应地调整相关玩法的难度及奖励。最多只能回退一级。#H等级调整后的24小时内，无法再次调整#E。等级调整不会影响角色等级上限。
en:
1. Level Breakthrough 
When the breakthrough conditions are met, you can perform a level breakthrough, and #Hyou can obtain a precious reward after each breakthrough#E. 

2. Level Impact 
As the solo mode level increases, #Hthe character level cap will also increase#E. Correspondingly, the level of some areas in the open world will increase, making the enemies stronger. The rewards obtained will also increase, including: #Hwild beasts, wild and outpost enemy strength and rewards for defeating them#E. 

3. Level Adjustment 
You can adjust the mode level. This includes level rollback and recovery, which will correspondingly adjust the difficulty and rewards of related gameplay. You can only roll back one level at most. #HWithin 24 hours after level adjustment, you cannot adjust again#E. Level adjustment will not affect the character level cap.

en:
Rivers flow beyond the realm of earth, and mountain hues shimmer between presence and absence. Sun Yuan once gazed upon the Scenic Scroll of the Three Hundred Miles of Jialing River. Inspired, he climbed to a high peak. In a moment of exhilaration, he wielded his fan with the flourish of splattered ink, as if painting with the mountains themselves, each stroke unstoppable, like a living landscape. But once the trance faded, he could never use that fan technique again.
Ten years passed. A bell chimed in the clouds. And in that instant, Sun Yuan recalled the feeling, and the Inkwell Fan resurfaced in the jianghu once more.

贫僧净玄，照影庙住持也。

近日有难民数众投宿本庙，多自荆湖逃难而来。入庙时已有数人高热不退，胸咳带血，身生赤疹。

今遣大弟子持信入城，恳请贵堂遣医者一二，携药来庙诊治。若不能至，亦望赐方药，使贫僧可依方救人。

en:
To the Benevolent Healers of Spring's Return Hall:

I am Jingxuan, Abbot of Reflection Temple.
Recently, a multitude of refugees have sought shelter in our temple, fleeing the disaster in Jinghu. Upon arrival, several already suffered from relentless fever, coughing up blood, and bearing red rashes on their flesh.
Yet our temple has neither healers nor medicine, and the sick continue to grow in number. My strength is spent. I fear once the plague fully erupts, the living will perish, and the dead will find no peace.
I send my eldest disciple into the city with this letter, begging your clinic to dispatch a healer or two with medicine to our temple. If you cannot come, please grant us a prescription and herbs, so I may attempt to save them.
The temple is impoverished, but we will offer what meager incense money we have in return. I beg the benevolent ones to take pity on these wandering souls of our chaotic times, and grant us your aid swiftly.

Abbot of Reflection Temple
#RLeave the temple.#E

zh:
第一次经过戏台的时候，父亲带着他，行路匆匆。
见孩子停下了脚步，父亲皱眉叹了口气：“就看一场。”

梨园弟子不常出现在这个小镇，偶尔能听到戏台奏响乐曲，比过年还让人开心。
不过如今世道，寻常百姓能有温饱已非易事，对年节也早没了念想，倒不如一戏一曲，以慰平生。
年幼的他，还看不明白戏台上演着怎样的故事。
梨树花落似雪，雪中一位紫铠将军，腰金执鞭独舞，指麾击刺。
戏散场，领头的一位像是师兄模样，带着年轻的弟子们拱手道谢，看到年幼的孩子，往他们手里塞一枚梨膏糖。

之后他被父亲牵着，到邻村远亲家中“暂住”。
靠着破旧薄被抵御春寒，天气一日日暖了。
烈日炎炎，耕田锄地，家中依旧杳无音信。

他摸着手臂被鞭打出的旧伤。
眼下秋收繁忙，没人看着他，正好设法回乡。

父母看见他出现在门口，眼中只有惊愕和懊恼。
家里的口粮不够，弟妹幼小，哥哥堪能劳作。
选择送走他，不费思量。
权衡生计利弊，目不识丁的人也能很快做出选择。
被赶走的看家犬会一次次回到旧居，但人只需要一个眼神，就能明白谁是被丢下的那个。
en:
The first time they passed the little roadside stage, his father was striding ahead, intent on getting where they were going. 
When the boy hesitated, the man stopped, frowned, and let out a long sigh. "...Fine. One performance." 

Masked Troupe disciples rarely visited a town this small. Whenever their music drifted through the streets, it brought more joy than the New Year ever did. 
But in times like these, when a full stomach was already a luxury, festivals had lost their shine. A single play, a single song—those were what comforted the living now. 
He was too young then to understand the story being told. 
He only remembered pear blossoms falling like snow, and in that snowfall, a general in violet armor—gold at his waist, whip in hand—dancing a lone, fierce dance of thrusts and strikes. 
When the show ended, the leader of the troupe—an older student, judging from his bearing—led the younger actors in a bow of thanks. Noticing the boy, he pressed a piece of pear-syrup candy into his palm. 

Soon after, his father took him to "stay for a while" with distant relatives in the next village. 
They braced against the spring chill with thin, fraying blankets, and day by day the air grew warmer. 
Under the harsh summer sun, the fields demanded tilling and hoeing, yet still no news came from home. 

He ran his fingers over the old whip scars on his arm. 
Now, with the autumn harvest in full swing and everyone occupied, no one was watching him. It seemed as good a time as any to make his way back. 

But when his parents saw him standing in their doorway, their eyes held only astonishment—and a certain troubled guilt. 
There wasn't enough grain. His younger siblings were too small. His older brother could work the fields. 
Sending him away had been the easiest choice, practically automatic. 
Even those who cannot read know how to weigh the cost of survival. 
A cast‑out dog might come back to its old home again and again—but a child needs only one look to understand exactly who was chosen and who was left behind.
Zheng Zongxian

zh:
高盛第一次见到马哭。
亡命途上，他们原本驾着两匹马昼夜奔逃，活活累死了一匹。
母亲淡淡地说，这马老了，当初另一匹诞下的时候还是喝它的奶长大的。
之后的路上，剩下的这匹小马便边跑边发出连绵不断的呜咽，被凛冽的罡风扯碎了在山谷间回荡，有如鬼哭。
马，也会有如此复杂的情感吗？
现在不是想这些的时候。
马的哀嚎声太响，会把追捕他们的杀手吸引过来，他们难逃一死。
高盛踏着马鞍欺身向前，把马嚼子用力塞紧，把马的悲鸣声硬生生堵在喉咙里。
身后的车帘里传来母亲威严的声音。
“这样它会憋死的，弃马弃车！”
听母亲的。
趁着马车在悬崖边拐弯，高盛条件反射般借力猛地抬脚，整架马车顺着陡峭的崖壁翻坠下去。与此同时，他搀着跃车而出的母亲矮身钻进崖壁上的天然石龛里。
他听到马悲怆的嘶鸣声远去，过了一会儿是追兵的马蹄声，一同没入深山中。

高盛用乱石封住龛口，这才惊魂稍定——若非母亲临机立断，他们难以险里逃生。杀手已然被那匹马尽数引走，短期内再无袭扰，只是要事在身，他们仍需尽快赶赴岱山。
山野归于死寂，母亲严肃道，“四下杀机未绝，寸步都要绷紧心神，如今我身边只剩你一个孩儿，你万万不能殒命，母亲自始至终都会护住你。”
她只微微抬手，高盛当即顺势俯身，将头安稳地侧枕在她膝上，好似一头猛兽温顺地俯首臣服。半晌，他闷闷应声：“儿定不会让母亲殒命。”
他与母亲本无血缘。
义母是久居深宫的奉陵宫人，而他昔日世家出身，一朝落难入宫为宦。凭一身出众的武艺，他屡受北司权贵笼络招揽，只为笼络他做一柄供人使唤的屠刀。可义母不一样。
他是深宫里无根的浮萍，母亲如一口沉静的幽潭般托举他飘摇的身骨，自己犯下弥天罪业，母亲本该厌弃疏远，可她依旧妥帖照拂、悉心教养，让他终日惶惶不安。
从此，听母亲的、信母亲的，成了刻进骨血的本能。
他伏在母亲膝前，一面听母亲念诵荐福祷文，一面回忆母亲半生对他的教诲。
“愿大行升遐，神驭安天……”
母亲教他一心向佛，佛非姑息慈悲，是以杀止杀、斩障护道。
“愿宗祧无倾，鼎祚永固……”
母亲教他一心向法，法非江湖私义，是皇室纲常、宗庙律令；
“愿四海清晏，烽燧尽息……”
母亲教他一心向李唐，非泛泛江山，而是先皇遗愿，东宫根脉。
他素来清楚自己同从前被母亲收留的诸多孩子别无二致，是宏大基业里一枚被妥善安放的棋子，多年来也一直甘之如饴。
母亲指尖徐徐落在他发间，梳他理散乱的发丝，轻声祷念：“愿此行岱山勘破秘宝实情。此前窃宝，虽触刑律，事出为公，乞佛祖垂怜宽宥。”
倏忽间一个念头攀上高盛心头——
岱山前路凶险莫测，倘若来日身陷死局，母亲当真会舍身护住自己吗？
他自己被这个念头吓住，猛地抬眼。
母亲当即停下梳发的手，垂眸轻问：“何事？”
高盛生怕被母亲发现心思，低声回道无事，把脑袋放回她的膝上。
紧绷的心弦一松，连日的疲惫涌上来，他神思涣散，竟昏昏沉沉睡了过去。

醒来时母亲已经睡下，他却警觉地闻到崖顶飘来的一股奇异肉香，和烤火的噼啪声。
是杀手去而复返？
高盛猛地起身，手已扣上腰畔长剑。
可比他动作更快的，是那熟悉的、鬼泣似的嘶鸣，裂破长空。
高盛纵身跃上悬崖，入目是一片猩红——
那匹引敌而去的小马竟奔了回来，鬃毛染血，双目赤红，铁蹄踏碎篝火，撞向正在大快朵颐的旅人，疯了似的蹄刨齿咬，浴血死斗。旅人们连声惨叫，棍棒刀器砸在马身上，它却半步不退，直至将旅人一一撞翻踏毙。
厮杀渐歇，那匹马也踉跄几步，轰然栽倒在地。
高盛这才发现，篝火上烤得焦黑的是马肉，旁边还有刚剥下的马皮，正是前几日累死、喂小马长大的乳母。想来是这群旅人在路边拾得老马尸身，贪一口肉食，落得这般横祸。
一匹马尚知回护哺育之恩，他受母亲多年照拂，却……

他的脸烧得滚烫，为方才有一瞬疑心大难临头母亲会弃他不顾而感到羞愧。
他竟敢有如此忤逆的想法。

躺在血泊里的马一息尚存，一双黑瞳望向他，犹在呜咽。
他心存怜惜，不自觉伸出手去，却听到母亲冷硬的命令：
“别管它，乘他们的马走。”
听母亲的。
高盛伸出一半的手猛地缩回，眼中闪过的温情转为木然，转身牵过旅人遗留的马。
他扶着母亲上鞍，随即翻身上马，一勒缰绳，朝着岱山方向，绝尘而去。
en:
Gao Sheng had never seen a horse weep until now.
Fleeing for their lives, they had driven their team without rest, day and night, until one of the beasts collapsed, its heart bursting from exhaustion.
"She was old," his mother murmured, her voice stripped of emotion. "When the young one was foaled, it was her milk that kept it alive."
On the road ahead, the surviving foal whimpered without end as it ran. The biting alpine wind shredded its cries, scattering them through the valley like the keening of ghosts.
Could a mere beast feel such profound grief?
There was no time to dwell on it.
The creature's mourning was so loud that it would draw the assassins straight to their necks.
Shifting his weight against the saddle, Gao Sheng lunged forward. He seized the bridle and jammed the bit violently into the horse's jaws, choking the tragic cries down its throat.
From behind the carriage curtain, his mother's voice cut through the wind with absolute authority.
"You will smother it. Abandon the carriage!"
He obeyed instantly.
As the carriage careened around a perilous cliffside bend, Gao Sheng's instincts took over. Anchoring his footing, he delivered a devastating kick, sending the entire coach hurtling over the precipice. In the same breath, he caught his mother as she vaulted from the plunging cabin, sweeping her into a natural stone alcove hidden within the rock face.
In the dark, he listened to the horse's despairing shrieks fade into the abyss below. Moments later, the thundering hooves of their pursuers swept past the ledge, swallowed by the depths of the mountains.

Gao Sheng hastily walled the alcove with loose stones, his racing heart finally beginning to settle. If not for his mother's ruthless, split-second judgment, they would be dead. The plummeting carriage had drawn the hounds away, buying them a fragile reprieve. But their burden remained heavy; they still had to reach Mount Tai, and quickly.
As a deathly silence reclaimed the wilderness, his mother spoke, her tone chillingly grave. "The woods are still crawling with blades. Keep your mind strung tight as a bowstring with every step. You are the only child I have left by my side. You cannot perish. I will protect you to the very end."
She raised her hand a fraction of an inch, and Gao Sheng yielded instantly. He lowered his head, resting it gently upon her lap like a feral beast tamed into utter submission. After a long time, his muffled voice broke the quiet: "I will never let you perish."
No blood bound them.
His adoptive mother was an ascetic of the Fengling Palace, a woman who had spent her life within the imperial walls. He, by contrast, was the ruined scion of a fallen noble house, cast into the labyrinth of the inner palace as a eunuch. Blessed with peerless martial skill, he was courted endlessly by the lords of the Northern Directorate, men who saw him as nothing more than a finely honed butcher's blade. But his mother was different.
He was but rootless driftweed in the vast, treacherous palace. She was the deep, unrippled pool that kept his fractured spirit afloat. Even when he committed the most monstrous sins, she did not recoil in disgust. Instead, she continued to shelter and nurture him with a meticulous grace that left him trembling with a profound, unsettled awe.
To obey her, to believe in her, had become an instinct carved into his very marrow.
Resting his head upon her lap, he listened to her softly chant the sutras of blessing, letting his mind drift back over a lifetime of her teachings.
"May the departed emperor ascend on high, his divine spirit calming the heavens..."
She taught him absolute devotion to the Buddha. But hers was not a Buddha of gentle mercy. It was a wrathful deity that wielded slaughter to end slaughter, cleaving through illusion to protect the Way.
"May the ancestral altars stand unbroken, the dynasty's reign endure eternal..."
She taught him absolute devotion to the Law. Not the vigilante justice of the jianghu, but the iron mandate of the imperial court and the sacred decrees of the ancestral shrines.
"May the realm know tranquility, the beacon fires of war burn no more..."
She taught him absolute devotion to the Tang Dynasty. Not to a vague notion of the realm, but to the late emperor's dying breath and the rightful bloodline of the Crown Prince.
He had long known that he was no different from the countless other orphans she had taken in over the years. He was merely a meticulously placed pawn upon a grand and terrible board. Yet, for years, he had swallowed this truth as though it were the sweetest wine.
Her fingertips traced slowly through his disheveled hair, smoothing the tangles as she breathed a quiet prayer: "May this journey to Mount Tai lay bare the truth of the hidden treasure. Though stealing the artifact defied the laws of the realm, it was done for a greater righteousness. I beg the Buddha for mercy and absolution."
A sudden, venomous thought coiled around Gao Sheng's heart.
The path to Mount Tai was shrouded in deadly peril. If the days ahead led them into an inescapable snare, would his mother truly trade her life for his?
Terrified by the treacherous nature of his own doubt, he jerked his head upward.
The hand in his hair stilled instantly. Lowering her gaze, she murmured, "What is it?"
Desperate to hide his racing thoughts, Gao Sheng muttered that it was nothing and let his head sink back onto her lap.
The moment the taut bowstring of his heart finally went slack, the crushing exhaustion of their relentless flight crashed over him. His mind drifted, scattering into the dark, until he surrendered to a heavy, dreamless sleep.

Gao Sheng awoke to find his mother already asleep, but a sudden, sharp instinct pulled him taut. Drifting down from the ridge above came the crackle of a campfire and the heavy, rich scent of roasting meat.
Had the hounds doubled back?
He was on his feet in a breath, his fingers locked around the hilt of his sword.
But before the blade could clear its sheath, a phantom wail, terrible and familiar, tore the night asunder.
Gao Sheng vaulted the cliff's edge. A slaughter awaited him.
The foal. The very beast that had plummeted into the abyss to lead their pursuers astray had somehow clawed its way back from the depths. Its mane was slick with gore, its eyes burning with a rabid, feverish red. With iron hooves, it scattered the campfire, hurling itself at the feasting scavengers in a blind frenzy. It was a tempest of snapping teeth and bone-crushing kicks, a blood-soaked fight to the bitter end. The men shrieked, bringing down clubs and blades in a desperate rain, but the animal did not yield a single inch. It fought until every last traveler lay trampled and broken in the ash.
When the carnage finally stilled, the horse faltered. It took a few trembling steps before collapsing heavily to the earth.
Only then did Gao Sheng look closely at the spit roasting over the scattered embers. It was charred horseflesh. Beside the fire lay a freshly flayed pelt, the remains of the old mare who had died of exhaustion days ago. The surrogate mother that had nursed this very foal. The travelers must have stumbled upon her carcass along the road, and in their greed for a free meal, invited their own grisly demise.
If a mere beast knew to lay down its life to avenge the mother that nursed it... He had been sheltered by his own mother for years, yet...

Gao Sheng's face burned with a sudden, searing shame. He had actually dared to doubt her. He had actually wondered, if only for a fleeting second, whether she would abandon him to save herself when the noose tightened.
How could he harbor such a treacherous, unfilial thought?

In the pooling blood, the young horse clung to a ragged breath. Its dark, glassy eyes found Gao Sheng, letting out a weak, agonizing whimper.
A rare pang of pity pierced his chest. Unconsciously, his hand reached out to comfort the dying creature...

"Leave it."
His mother's voice cut through the dark, cold and unyielding as iron. "Take their horses. Let's go."
To obey her was instinct.
The hand that was halfway extended snapped back to his side. The brief flicker of warmth in his eyes died, freezing over into a hollow, wooden apathy. Turning his back on the dying beast, he gathered the reins of the dead men's surviving mounts.
He hoisted his mother into the saddle, then vaulted onto his own. With a sharp crack of the reins, they vanished into the night toward Mount Tai, leaving nothing behind but the silence of the dead.
Ying Xu

zh:
裴文远喜欢听老兵说起长安。
他听说长安的流水潺潺，载着风月，流过亭台楼馆。
他亦听老兵们说，曲江池的芙蓉虽艳，比不上国色天香的牡丹。
裴文远低下头。他没见过牡丹，也没去过长安。
“以后……我也要去长安看看。”少年的眼中亮起光。
烽烟血尘中，裴文远眼中的光芒飘摇欲灭。
鲜血如花一样肆意绽放在每一位战士身上，不分敌我。

“牡丹的颜色……也这般鲜艳么？”
“牡丹的味道……也这样浓烈么？”
“牡丹的温度……也这样……炙热么？”
颈中鲜血喷洒，裴文远感觉体温正在迅速离开自己。
他的血，亦绽放成了一朵牡丹。
他最后看到的，是视野里飞溅的红，仿佛长安群芳摇曳的春。
en:
Pei Wenyuan loved to listen to the tales veterans told about Chang'an.
He imagined the gentle streams carrying the breeze and moonlight past elegant pavilions and grand halls.
They said the lotus was beautiful, but no match for the exquisite peony, the "beauty of the nation."
Pei looked down. He'd never seen a peony nor even been to Chang'an.
"One day, I want to see Chang'an too," he said, eyes shining with hope.
But amid the smoke and blood of war, that light flickered, fragile and faint.
Blood bloomed across every soldier's body, friend and foe alike.

"Is the peony's color... truly this vivid?"
"Is its fragrance... just as intense?"
"Is its warmth... this fiercely burning?"
As blood spilled from his neck, Pei felt his life draining fast.
His blood blossomed into a peony.
The last thing he saw was red splattered before his eyes, like spring flowers swaying in the gardens of Chang'an, full of life and fleeting beauty.

en:
Lesson: Words That'll Trip You Up
Down here, some words sound so close you might mix 'em up if you ain't careful. Folks might laugh, but it's all in good fun. Here's a few that get even locals tangled sometimes:

Pen and Pin
Say 'em slow: "I lost my pen" and "I stuck it with a pin." Down here, those sound almost like twins!

Hill and Heel
Walk up the hill, or your boot's got a heel? Sometimes, you got to listen close to tell one from the other.

Feel and Fill
You might say "I feel the cup" when you meant to say "I fill the cup." Happens to the best of us.

Practice sayin' each pair a few times, first slow, then faster. If you got a friend from around here, see if they can spot the difference when you say 'em.

And if Old Egg barks when you say "hill," but not when you say "heel," you know you're gettin' somewhere!

少东家快来找我喝酒：
我心里堵得慌，不找你喝两杯吐吐苦水，怕是要憋出病来。
出游在外，才知道还是俺们清河人实在。我在开封街上撞上一位仙女儿一样的女侠。我都没敢看人家，是人家主动跟我搭话，说瞧着我憨厚，想跟我处对象过日子。我当时想俺这不是做梦吧！
结果，相处了没几日，她却让门中师弟给我送了封信，说要跟城西的张镖头处对象，醉花阴的门规，得告知我一声，让我 “知悉便可”。
我当时就懵了，啥门规啊还管这个？跑去问她，她让俺莫急：“赵大哥，醉花阴门规说，侠缘可择多位，但若有新动向，需如实告知旧人，这是对彼此的尊重。” 
我寻思着或许是误会，还想再争取争取，结果没过三天，又收到她的口信，说要跟城南的李书生处对象，依旧是 “按门规告知”。
我去打听，才明白，合着我不是她唯一的侠缘！算上我，她前前后后找了五个！
五个也就五个吧，谁叫人醉花阴的就这个规矩……我正准备一大家子以后好好过日子，结果她权衡一下，说我跟人撞型了，独独把俺断舍离了！
少东家你说这叫什么事儿啊！若是你得空，务必来和我喝上一杯，咱想跟你说说心里话。

赵大力留
en:
Young Master, come drink with me:
My heart is so heavy. If I don't have a few drinks and vent to you, I think I'm going to get sick.
Traveling abroad, I realized that only us folks from Qinghe are truly honest. I bumped into a heroine in Kaifeng who looked like a celestial fairy. I didn't even dare look at her, but she approached me first, saying I looked honest and she wanted to date me and settle down. I thought I was dreaming!
But after only a few days, she had her junior brother send me a letter, saying she was going to date Escort Leader Zhang from the west side of the city. She said the rules of the Velvet Shade require her to let me know "for my information."
I was baffled. What kind of sect rule is that? I ran to ask her, and she told me not to worry: "Big Zhao, the Velvet Shade rules say we can choose multiple partners, but if there's a new development, we must truthfully inform the old ones. It's out of respect for each other."
I thought it might be a misunderstanding and wanted to try harder, but not even three days later, I got another message saying she was going to date Scholar Li from the south side, again "informed as per sect rules."
I asked around and finally understood. It turns out I wasn't her only partner! Including me, she had five!
Five is fine, I guess, if that's just the Velvet Shade way... I was getting ready for us all to live happily as one big family, but then she weighed things up and said I overlapped with someone else's "type," so she optimized me out!
Young Master, can you believe this?! If you have time, you must come have a drink with me. I really need a heart-to-heart.

Yours, Zhao Dali

en:
Zhang Wanshi was awarded the title of Grand Artisan at age nineteen. At nineteen, diligent disciples usually just qualify to enter the Inner Sect.
At that time, Zhang Wanshi's brilliance was at its peak. He claimed to know all devices, capable of being a teacher to thousands of disciples to come, needing no borrowed name from sages. He insisted on using his own name as the Grand Artisan title, which caused much controversy.
Later, when Raven was awarded a title, Zhang Wanshi was already waiting outside the hall.
I just suddenly remembered, today you receive your title, Master should give a gift. But our Master is rarely home, so I shall do it for him. Here, freshly cast. A sharp sword hidden in an archaic sheath. "Victory Sword."

Zhang Wanshi knew his junior brother would surely return in victory.
And Raven understood that his senior brother never imposed his own will upon others.

唐·杜甫
八月秋高风怒号，卷我屋上三重茅。茅飞渡江洒江郊，高者挂罥长林梢，下者飘转沉塘坳。
南村群童欺我老无力，忍能对面为盗贼。公然抱茅入竹去，唇焦口燥呼不得，归来倚杖自叹息。
俄顷风定云墨色，秋天漠漠向昏黑。布衾多年冷似铁，娇儿恶卧踏里裂。床头屋漏无干处，雨脚如麻未断绝。自经丧乱少睡眠，长夜沾湿何由彻！
安得广厦千万间，大庇天下寒士俱欢颜。风雨不动安如山！呜呼，何时眼前突兀见此屋，吾庐独破受冻死亦足！
en:
Du Fu (Tang Dynasty)
In the eighth moon, the autumn wind howls high and strong, tearing three layers of thatch from my roof along; some thatch flies over the river and spreads on the shore, some hangs on the treetops, and some sinks to the muddy ground.
The village children mock my age and weakness, steal my thatch into the bamboos with boldness; my lips are dry, my shouts are all in vain, I come back leaning on my staff and sigh around.
Soon the wind stops, clouds turn dark, the autumn sky is gloomy and black; my quilt is cold as iron for years, my kid sleeps badly and tears the bed in fears; the roof leaks, no dry spot remains, the rain drips like hemp threads without end; since the war, I've had little sleep. How can I get through this long night?
Oh for a mansion of thousands of rooms, to shelter all poor scholars with happy blooms; unmoved by wind and rain, it stands like a mountain! Alas, when shall I see such a house before my eyes? Then my own hut may break and I may freeze, but I would be content to die in such a light!

Pure heart without flaw, utmost clarity without stain; wisdom sun, Buddha light, illuminating and breaking all darkness.

With peace regained in Liangzhou and Hexi, the Purity Pagoda quietly awaits the day Buddha's light reappears.

#Y$SN#E，这趟出门，鹅不光没花完你给的钱，还替你摸索出了一条“生财门道”。

前些时，鹅在这个叫一百条鱼的地方游历，偶然间碰见了一位穿绿衣服的游侠，那小嘴叭叭，一开口鹅就知道定是名门弟子。

他一眼就看穿了本鹅非同凡鹅，就跟鹅谈了个合作——他先把鹅“卖”给附近的食肆，等拿到钱，他再助鹅从后厨偷溜，到时候收益五五分账。

聪明鹅一听就懂，看似是卖鹅，实则就是你常挂在嘴边的“可持续发财”嘛！

头几回发财都顺溜极了。掌柜的付钱爽快，后厨的门栓也好撬。鹅还分到了好多铜板，沉甸甸的，都寄存在绿衣小弟那儿了，他说要帮鹅先攒着，以免鹅裤兜浅，路上弄丢。

#Y$SN#E，说来你也会羡慕鹅的好命！最近绿衣小弟说要回乡奔丧，将鹅托付给他一个朋友先照顾着享福。鹅现在每天都有人给按摩拍背，就连夜里睡觉的小窝都是花瓣并香料搭成的！

就说今天吧，那人还特地给鹅准备了热水澡，外加什么“马杀鹅”服务。

#Y$SN#E，你就等鹅这趟“休养”结束吧，等鹅享完了福，一定带着钱风风光光回家！

先不说了，热水快烧开了，咕嘟咕嘟的……鹅要先去泡澡啦！下次再给你讲鹅的江湖传说！

聪明鹅留
en:
Honk, honk honk! Honk honk honk? Honk honk honk... Honk, honk honk (Puts wings on its hips and wiggles its butt smugly). Honk honk!
...
#Y$SN#E, on this trip, not only did I not spend all the money you gave me, but I also figured out a way to make a fortune.
A while ago, while traveling through a place called A Hundred Fish, I bumped into a wanderer in green. The way he talked, I knew right away he was a disciple from a prestigious sect.
He saw at a glance that I am no ordinary goose and proposed a partnership. He would "sell" me to a nearby eatery, take the money, and then help me sneak out the back. We'd split the profits fifty-fifty.
This smart goose understood immediately. It looks like selling a goose, but it's actually that "sustainable wealth" you always talk about!
The first few times went perfectly. The bosses paid up quickly, and the kitchen latches were easy to pick. I got a lot of heavy copper coins. I left them with my green-clad sidekick; he said he'd save them for me so I wouldn't lose them on the road since my pockets are shallow.
#Y$SN#E, you'd be jealous of my good luck! Recently, my green-clad sidekick said he had to return home for a funeral and entrusted me to a friend of his to enjoy life. Now, I have someone massaging my back every day, and even my bed at night is made of petals and spices!
Just today, that guy prepared a hot bath especially for me, plus some kind of "Massa-goose" service.
#Y$SN#E, just wait until my "vacation" is over. Once I've enjoyed myself enough, I'll definitely come home with the money in glory!
Gotta go, the hot water is almost boiling, bubbling away... I'm going to take my bath first! I'll tell you more of my Jianghu legends next time!
Yours, The Smart Goose

zh:
【序】
前段日子总见着几个相约浣衣的阿婆路过门口时驻足片刻，却不入内问诊。我心生好奇，上前搭话，才注意到她们指尖皲裂。我问阿婆们为何不入内问诊，阿婆局促地笑笑，答道：“不过是在河里用冷水洗衣，冻裂了些口子，忍忍也便罢了。瞧病的几个铜板，若拿去换盐，够家里吃上许久。”我心中发酸，于是起了写这本薄方的念头。
【病症：凉水裂手】
原方：当归二钱、紫草二钱，忍冬藤一钱，麻油一斤熬膏。
评：紫草昂贵，更不必说一斤麻油之价。
薄方：花椒二钱，生姜三片，艾叶二钱，当归一钱。水二升，煎三沸，去渣，趁热泡手。花椒、当归略贵，可买碎末贱者，效果无差。生姜厨下即有，艾叶河埠可采。
试验：阿婆们知我试方，皆笑着伸手。起先我还怕药效不好，但阿婆泡手后，笑说这花椒辣手，手上热乎乎的，疼痛反倒是缓解了几分。几日之后，阿婆们来回春堂门口找我，让我抄了几份“辣辣的花椒水方子”，说要带回去让家中识字的晚辈抓药去。

有个阿婆又来寻我，说家中老头子做船工，身上的红疹子忍了许多年，夜无安眠。阿婆信我，问我有什么草药方子能缓解。
【病症：湿疹瘙痒】
原方：麻黄四钱、桂枝二钱、杏仁三钱、白术三钱、炙甘草二钱。九碗水，先煮麻黄去沫，再下诸药，煎至二碗半，分三次服。
评：此方加工繁琐，耗时费力。船工师傅们披星戴月地忙活，日日煎服，哪来的闲工夫？且湿疹在表面，汤药入腹，起效太慢。
薄方：马齿苋一把，鲜者捣烂更佳，苦参二钱，花椒一钱，艾叶二钱。水三升，煎三沸，去渣，温洗患处，勿抓。马齿苋、艾叶堤岸边常见，其余草药亦可买碎末贱者，此法或可行。
试验：过了几日，阿婆便回来与我说，老头子的病有所缓解，瘙痒感减弱，晚上能睡个整觉，干活也更有力气了。我想着，或许把药水浸湿麻布，得空时外敷更方便，只是今日堂内事务重，还未能告诉阿婆。

前几日去茶楼吃茶，发现店中小二来往奔走，十分疲乏。我观他腿肚似有浮肿，应有筋瘤前兆。想来城中营生如此之人，何止一二？念及于此，我当即折返，决意搜罗古籍验方，研拟一剂舒筋活络之法。
【病症：久站腿肿】
原方：《刺节真邪》有云：“筋屈不得伸，邪气居其间而不反，发为筋瘤。”常用的均是些刺络放血、针灸的诊疗方子。
评：这些方子效果虽好，但有此症结的多为各店中佣人，终日奔忙，更无余钱医治。最好有药茶方子，随手就能饮几口，稍缓疲乏。
薄方：橘核二钱，益母草二钱，黑豆五钱。水三升，煎三沸，去渣，代茶温饮。橘核理气散结，益母草活血利水，黑豆补肾消肿。三味平和，可常服。
试验：我回医堂后连试数剂，最终定下这方子，价格实惠，寻常人家也能时常饮用。虽无法根治症结，能缓解疼痛已是大善。日后若是得闲，或许可以与堂中同僚商量，支个小茶摊，煮些药茶送给路过百姓，也是善事一件了。
en:
[Preface]
Some days back, I kept noticing several elderly women, gathered for washing clothes together, pausing briefly outside my door as they passed, yet never coming in to seek treatment. Curious, I approached and struck up conversation, and only then did I notice their fingertips, cracked and chapped. When I asked why they would not come in for a consultation, one of the grannies smiled awkwardly and said: "It's only from washing clothes in the cold river water—the skin cracks a bit, but bearing it is enough. A few copper coins spent on seeing a physician could instead buy salt enough to feed the household for a good while." My heart ached to hear it, and so I resolved to compile this modest little formulary.
[Illness: Hands Cracked by Cold Water]
Original Prescription: Angelica, two qian; Gromwell root, two qian; Honeysuckle vine, one qian; simmered into a paste with one jin of sesame oil.
Comment: Gromwell root is costly, let alone the price of a full jin of sesame oil.
Simplified Prescription: Sichuan Peppercorn, two qian; Ginger, three slices; Mugwort leaf, two qian; Angelica, one qian. Boil in two sheng of water until it comes to a boil three times, strain out the dregs, and soak the hands while still warm. Peppercorn and Angelica are somewhat costly, but one may buy the cheaper crushed remnants with no difference in effect. Ginger is found in any kitchen, and Mugwort leaf may be gathered along the riverbank.
Trial: When the grannies learned I meant to test the remedy, they all laughed and held out their hands. At first I feared the medicine might prove weak, but after soaking their hands, they laughed, saying the peppercorn stung a little, yet their hands grew warm, and the pain eased noticeably. A few days later, the grannies came looking for me outside Spring's Return Hall, asking me for a few copies of the "spicy peppercorn water recipe" for them, saying they wished to bring it home for the literate younger ones to gather the herbs themselves.

Another granny came seeking me again, saying that her old husband, a boatman, had endured red rashes upon his skin for many years, and could find no peaceful sleep at night. Trusting in me, she asked if there were any herbal remedy that might bring him relief.
[Illness: Itching Eczema]
Original Prescription: Ephedra, four qian; Cinnamon Twig, two qian; Almond, three qian; Bai Zhu, three qian; roasted Licorice, two qian. Nine bowls of water—first boil the Ephedra and skim off the foam, then add the remaining herbs, and simmer down to two and a half bowls, to be taken in three doses.
Comment: This prescription is troublesome to prepare, consuming much time and effort. Boatmen labor from before dawn until after dusk—where would they find the leisure to brew and drink it daily? Moreover, the eczema lies upon the skin's surface, while a decoction taken internally acts far too slowly.
Simplified Prescription: A handful of Purslane, mashed fresh for best effect; Sophora root, two qian; Sichuan Peppercorn, one qian; Mugwort leaf, two qian. Boil in three sheng of water until it comes to a boil three times, strain out the dregs, and wash the afflicted area while warm—do not scratch. Purslane and Mugwort leaf are commonly found along the embankments, and the remaining herbs may likewise be bought as cheaper crushed remnants; this method may well serve.
Trial: A few days later, the granny returned to tell me that her husband's condition had eased—the itching had lessened, he could now sleep through the night undisturbed, and he had grown more vigorous at his work. I thought that perhaps soaking hemp cloth in the medicinal water for external application in spare moments might prove even more convenient, though with the hall's affairs pressing heavily upon me today, I have not yet had the chance to tell the granny so.

A few days ago, I went to a teahouse for tea, and noticed the waiter running to and fro, utterly worn out. I observed some swelling about his calves, likely the early sign of a tendon knot. It occurred to me that in this city, those who toil at such trades must number far more than one or two. Struck by this thought, I turned back at once, resolved to search through old medical texts for a tried formula, and devise a remedy to relax the sinews and quicken the flow.
[Illness: Swollen Legs from Prolonged Standing]
Original Prescription: The Needling Jie: True and Evil Qi states: "When the sinews bend and cannot extend, and pernicious energy lodges within without retreating, a tendon knot forms." The usual treatments are bloodletting by pricking the vessels, and acupuncture.
Comment: Though these methods are effective, most who suffer from this affliction are servants at various shops, laboring ceaselessly all day, with no spare coin for treatment. Better to have an herbal tea recipe that may be sipped at any spare moment, to ease the fatigue somewhat.
Simplified Prescription: Tangerine seed, two qian; Motherwort, two qian; Black soybean, five qian. Boil in three sheng of water until it comes to a boil three times, strain out the dregs, and drink warm in place of tea. Tangerine seed regulates the qi and dissolves stagnation; Motherwort invigorates the blood and promotes water flow; Black soybean nourishes the kidneys and reduces swelling. All three are mild in nature and may be taken regularly.
Trial: Back at the medical hall, I tried several variations before settling upon this recipe—inexpensive enough for ordinary households to drink often. Though it cannot cure the root affliction, easing the pain alone is already a fine mercy. If time allows in days to come, perhaps I might discuss with my colleagues at the hall the idea of setting up a small tea stall, brewing herbal tea to offer to passing commoners—that too would be a worthy deed.

伊刀始终知道，同行江湖，总有分别的一天。
他已经对此十分娴熟。
只是没想到，这一天来得如此之快。
